data.description:
## Incident Overview

When an agent in a host project (parity-scan, plugin v1.13.0) hits the `record-test-status-guard` PreToolUse hook because of an unprefixed direct call to `record-test-status.sh`, the hook output mixes the legitimate guard message with a bash error from `pre-bash.sh:139`, making the message hard to read and triggering follow-on confusion.

## Reproducer

In a host project with the v1.13.0 plugin cache, running:

```
DSO_COMMIT_WORKFLOW=1 bash $HOME/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/digital-service-orchestra/plugins/dso/hooks/record-test-status.sh
```

Produces:

```
PreToolUse:Bash hook error: [\${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/run-hook.sh dispatchers/pre-bash.sh]: BLOCKED [record-test-status-guard]: Direct calls to record-test-status.sh are not allowed.
Test status is recorded automatically by the test gate during commits.
If you need to transfer test status from a worktree, use harvest-worktree.sh (--attest flag).
/Users/<user>/.claude/plugins/cache/digital-service-orchestra/dso/1.13.0/hooks/dispatchers/pre-bash.sh: line 139: : No such file or directory
/Users/<user>/.claude/plugins/cache/digital-service-orchestra/dso/1.13.0/hooks/dispatchers/pre-bash.sh: line 139: return: can only \`return' from a function or sourced script
```

## Expected vs Observed

**Expected:** When the guard blocks an unprefixed call, the agent should see only the guard message + DSO_COMMIT_WORKFLOW=1 hint, with no spurious bash errors.

**Observed:** Two bash errors from `pre-bash.sh:139` appear after the guard message, suggesting an empty/unset variable expansion + `return` outside a function context. The message structure suggests the dispatcher hit an error path after blocking, rather than exiting cleanly.

## Bug Scope

The bug is the spurious `pre-bash.sh:139` errors after the guard fires, NOT the failure to record test status when improperly called. The guard correctly blocks the call; the dispatcher just emits noisy bytes after.

## Proposed Investigation

Inspect `plugins/dso/hooks/dispatchers/pre-bash.sh` line 139 in v1.13.0; confirm whether the early-exit path uses `return` outside a sourced context or expands an unset var without quoting. Likely a missing `exit` vs `return` cleanup after the guard verdict.
data.title: [pre-bash.sh hook]: BLOCKED record-test-status-guard message contains line 139 errno -> agent confused by spurious error
